note: Catalogue capture for the held tier-5 English Wikipedia article 'Leclerc (tank)'. The article is a secondary compilation, so every value is grade claimed and the registry marks primary_held false. It holds the Leclerc main battle tank as a tracked entry. It publishes identity, the Series 1 mass with the Series 2 and Series XXI masses as separate configurations, the overall length, width and height, the ground clearance, the engine model and rating, the automatic transmission, the maximum road speed, the road range and the fording and wading depths. It publishes no track shoe width, no track pitch and no grouser statement, so the entry is not runtime-ready.

operating_weight_kg.locator: Infobox, Specifications section, Mass row, Series 1 entry
operating_weight_kg.state: mass published for Series 1 as 54.5 tonnes; recorded as 54,500 kg with the tonne taken as 1,000 kg; the same row publishes Series 2 at 56.3 tonnes and Series XXI at 57.4 tonnes as separate configurations, and the article states no kerb or gross weight

length_mm.state: overall length with the gun, published as 9.87 m (6.88 m without gun); the published metre figure used directly

width_mm.state: width published as 3.60 m; the technical data table publishes 3.43 m for the hull and 3.71 m with side-view mirrors as separate configurations

height_mm.state: height to the turret roof, published as 2.53 m; the published metre figure used directly

ground_clearance_mm.locator: Technical data table, Ground clearance row
ground_clearance_mm.state: ground clearance published as 500 mm; the published millimetre figure used directly

fording_depth_mm.locator: Technical data table, Wading depth without preparation row
fording_depth_mm.state: fording depth without preparation, published as a wading depth of 1.1 m; the published metre figure used directly

wading_depth_mm.locator: Technical data table, Wading depth with snorkel row
wading_depth_mm.state: wading depth with snorkel, published as 4 m; the published metre figure used directly

engine_model.state: engine published as a V8X SACM (Wartsila) eight-cylinder diesel; the article prints the maker name with the a-diaeresis letter, recorded here in ASCII

published_power_hp.state: engine published as 1,100 kW (1,500 hp), with no net basis

max_speed_kmh.locator: Infobox, Specifications section, Maximum speed row
max_speed_kmh.state: maximum road speed, published as 71 km/h (44 mph) on the road; the same row publishes 55 km/h (34 mph) off-road as a separate state

range_km.locator: Infobox, Specifications section, Operational range row
range_km.state: operational range, published as 550 km (342 mi); the same row publishes 650 km (404 mi) with external fuel as a separate state
